title: One
text:
She is tall and perfect, with radiating blue

pupils, where an Eve lazily lies in wait.

Her skin is fruit skin. Her white flesh snows

and her braids twist like thick eels.


A forest of gold grows in her white armpits.

From the trees breaks the fine new bud.

Her mouth is death's tenebrous cave.

her laughter wounds the breast of tranquil birds.


Yesterday she passed by my side, round hips,

hard tense thighs lifting the lace,

purpled lips, and I was afraid to see her,


for she is in such a way already predestined

that, one understands, on seeing her, she walks, abandoned,

toward the first man who must possess her.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the disturbing predestination of the erotic portrait.

title: I Walk Slowly Along the Acacia Path...
text:
I walk slowly along the acacia path,

their snow petals perfume my hands,

my hair grows restless under a light zephyr

and the soul is like foam of aristocracies.


Good genius: this day you favor me,

hardly a sigh makes me eternal and brief...

Am I about to fly now that the soul moves?

Wings grow on my feet and the three Graces dance.


It is that last night your hands, in my hands of fire,

gave so many sweetnesses to my blood, that afterward,

my mouth filled with perfumed honeys.


So fresh that in the clean dawn of Summer

I greatly fear turning back running to the hamlet

with golden butterflies caught on my lips.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the classical lightness of Graces, zephyr, honey, and butterflies.

title: Despite Myself I Love You; You Are So Vain...
text:
Despite myself I love you; you are as vain

as handsome, and pride, vigilant, tells me:

"For this you chose? Low is your taste;

do not sell yourself for anything, not even for a Roman profile"


And desire, dark and pagan, dictates to me

to open in you a wide gash through which your vital

murmur would be strained... Only dead, my lullaby

would wrap you more sweetly, seeking mouth and hand.


Salomé reborn? My gestures are poorer.

These are bad times already for tragic things.

I am she who always lives her life incomplete.


For she does not lose her line for a Greek feast

and to undecided chance, undulating, she bends

with distant eyes and distracted soul.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the dramatic Salomé fantasy undercut by modern incompletion.

title: Under Their Red Backs, in the Dark Mahogany...
text:
Under their red spines, in the dark mahogany,

Your books sleep. I follow the latest authors:

Other forms attract me, other new colors

And the current steals me toward your pagan feasts.


I enjoy fierce styles — wide wolf teeth.

Others sober, meticulous — watchful cypresses.

Others white and fine — columns beneath flowers.

Others acidic and ocher — bedroom storms.


I had already forgotten you and by chance I take you up again,

And at the first verses there rises from the volume

Your fresh and fine breath of fragrant honeys.


Lover to whom one returns as the first time:

You are the sweet mouth that back there, in spring,

Liquefied in our veins an entire forest of roses.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the poem as a reading encounter that becomes erotic return.

title: Love
text:
Seven Lives

To Mrs. María A. S. de Fontán


I have seven lives, I have seven lives.

Seven lives of gold;

lovely and florid.

Head cut off, head replaced:

My tree-spirit

sprouts again in the siesta.


Purple dragon of flowering claws,

seven lives I have, I have seven

lives.

Giants and dwarfs: cut off my heads,

they will grow stubborn as

the weeds.


I have seven lives, I have seven lives,

seven lives of gold lovely and

florid


that irons tire and swords notch,

yet one day they will be forever

felled.


The prince I await will dry

the seven flowering heads. Without

abracadabras,

the winged dragon will lose its lives

beneath the slender edge of

sweet words.
editorial_note: The catalog title says Love, but the embedded source is Seven Lives, so the internal heading is preserved.

title: The Deception
text:
I am yours, God knows why, since I understand

that you will abandon me, coldly, tomorrow,

and that beneath the charm of my eyes, desire

is won by another charm, but I do not defend myself.


I wait for this to end on any given day,

for I intuit, instantly, what you think or want.

With indifferent voice I speak to you of other women

and even rehearse the praise of one who was yours.


But you know less than I, and somewhat proud

that I belong to you, in your deceptive game

you persist, with the air of an actor owning the role.


I look at you silently with my sweet smile,

and when you grow enthusiastic, I think: do not hurry.

It is not you who deceives me; what deceives me is my dream.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the speaker's lucid awareness that the real deception is self-made.

title: Wait
text:
I must give you my hands, wait, still

the earth is full of the murmur of day.

The celestial vault lets none

of its stars be seen... the moon sleeps in the heavens.


I must give you my hands, but wait, for now

everything thinks and works —life is foresighted—

But my heart hides solitary,

disconsolate and sad from the daily bustle.


It is necessary that everything that moves gain

a vague laziness, that effort founder,

that a tranquil rest fall over the world,

an all-sweet, consoling and meek medium.


Wait... sweetly, balsamic with calm,

night will arrive, I will give you my hands,

but now those worldly noises prevent it;

there is too much light, I cannot see your soul.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the deferred intimacy until night quiets the world.

title: The Endless
text:
It is not your fault if in your hands

my love lost its petals like a rose:

Spring will come and there will be flowers...

the dry trunk will give new leaves.


The tears shed will become pearls

of a new necklace; shadow will be broken by

a precious sun that will give to the veins

fresh sap, mad and bubbling.


You will follow your route; I mine

and both, freed, like butterflies

will lose the pollen from our wings

and find more pollen in the flora.


Words dry up like rivers

and kisses dry up like roses,

but for every death seven lives

seek lips demanding dawn.


But... what was? It is never recovered!

And every spring that sketches itself

is one more corpse that acquires life

and one more bud that loses its petals!
editorial_note: The translation preserves the regenerative argument and the final refusal of full recovery.

title: The Causeless Caress Slips from My Fingers...
text:
The caress without cause slips from my fingers,

slips from my fingers... In the wind, as it passes,

the caress that wanders without destiny or object,

the lost caress—who will gather it?


I could love tonight with infinite pity,

I could love the first one who happened to arrive.

No one arrives. The flowered paths are alone.

The lost caress will roll... will roll...


If in your eyes they kiss you tonight, traveler,

if a sweet sighing shivers the branches,

if a small hand presses your fingers

that takes you and leaves you, that wins you and goes away.


If you do not see that hand, nor that mouth that kisses,

if it is the air that weaves the illusion of kissing,

oh, traveler, whose eyes are like the sky,

melted into the wind, will you recognize me?
editorial_note: The translation keeps the caress as an airborne, ownerless gesture seeking recognition.

title: Dead Soul
text:
Huge stones, red sun and dust

raised in clouds over dry earth...

The sun, as it left, murmured in my ear:

you have your soul never dead.


Moving serpents at my side

raised their heads to my mouth.

The gray sky, the stone, repeated:

you have your soul never dead.


Vulture beaks were felt later

beside my feet stirring the earth;

voices of the plain the afternoon repeated:

you have your soul never dead.


Oh fertile sun, enflamed earth,

starry sky, enormous sea, forest,

enter my soul, shake it.

This poor one sleeps who seems dead.


Ah, may your eyes awaken, soul,

and find the world as something new...

Ah, may your eyes awaken, soul,

soul that sleeps with a dead smell...
editorial_note: The translation keeps the strange repeated assurance that the soul is never dead.
